newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Malev looking to lease Fokkers.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Malev looking to lease Fokkers.

text.p: Hungary's national airline Malev Rt said on Monday it was looking to lease two Fokker 70 short range airliners from an unnamed European company, but no additional details were available.
"After our annual general meeting on December 16, our plans will be fixed," Malev spokesperson Gabor Peterffy told Reuters.
Malev said earlier it planned to expand its fleet in March 1997, but it was not clear on Monday whether the expansion will include new planes beyond the two Fokkers.
The fleet currently includes 14 Boeings (six B737-200s, four B737-300s, two B737-400s and two B767-200ERs), three Fokker 70s and 10 Tupolevs (seven Tu-154s and three Tu-134s).

Malev is owned 63.9 percent by the Hungarian Privatisation and Asset Holding Co (APV Rt), 30.0 percent by Italian national airline Alitalia, 5.0 percent by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Trade's investment agency SIMEST and 1.1 percent by other interests, including Hungarian municipalities.
